findings.body:
**Fix the `attribution` doc so it matches the implemented witness.**

Line 662 says `trusted` means "the report's first reviewed head equals the admitted head". The implementation at Line 875–881 uses only `report.admissionHead`. The header at Line 32–35 and the `ReviewAddressReport.admissionHead` doc (src/ops/review/address.ts:144-248) both say explicitly that `rounds[].record.head` is mutable and must not be used. This exported type doc is the contract that consumers read, so it points them to the rejected evidence.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-  /** `trusted` only when the report's first reviewed head equals the admitted head. */
+  /** `trusted` only when the report's immutable `admissionHead` equals the candidate's admitted head. */
   attribution: 'trusted' | 'unattributed' | 'absent';
```
</details>
findings.title: Fix the `attribution` doc so it matches the implemented witness.

findings.body:
**Report `deferredVendorDebt: 'unknown'` when no report exists.**

Line 925 maps `report === undefined` to `'absent'`. Line 843 and Line 856 hardcode `'absent'` for exception rows and not-admitted rows. Those rows have no report, so the planner has no evidence that debt is absent. Two cases are at risk:

- A `failed` or `indeterminate` leg that returned no `report`.
- A leg that threw after it began work.

In both cases the leg can leave durable author debt. The row then says that the debt is affirmatively absent.

The module header states the rule "no attributable head is a non-success, never invented". The `'unknown'` member already exists in the type, so the planner has a truthful value for this case. A consumer that filters rows on `deferredVendorDebt === 'present'` or `!== 'absent'` silently skips these rows.

A not-admitted leg never ran. For that leg, `'absent'` is defensible. A thrown leg and a report-less settled leg need `'unknown'`.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
     const debt: AddressManyRow['deferredVendorDebt'] =
-      report === undefined
-        ? 'absent'
-        : trusted
+      trusted
           ? report.deferredVendorDebt === undefined
             ? 'absent'
             : 'present'
           : 'unknown';
```

Apply the same change at Line 843 (exception row): `deferredVendorDebt: 'unknown'`. With this change, Line 933 also emits the "debt state unknowable" reason for report-less legs. Reword that reason so it does not say "at an unattributed head" when no report exists.
</details>
findings.title: Report `deferredVendorDebt: 'unknown'` when no report exists.

findings.body:
**Fix `relevant()`: it compares the whole `scripts` object, not only install lifecycle scripts.**

`scripts` is in `descriptiveManifestFields`, so `relevant()` removes it. Lines 171-172 add it back as the full `parsed.scripts` object when any key is an install lifecycle script. Many repositories have a `prepare` script, for example husky.

A PR that edits an unrelated script such as `scripts.test` then makes `isDeepStrictEqual` fail at Line 178. The error says that the manifests or locks differ, and the user must reinstall. This contradicts the intent of the descriptive-field filter.

Keep only the lifecycle keys:

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    if (Object.keys(parsed.scripts ?? {}).some((key) => installLifecycleScripts.has(key)))
-      fields.scripts = parsed.scripts;
+    const lifecycle = Object.fromEntries(
+      Object.entries(parsed.scripts ?? {}).filter(([key]) => installLifecycleScripts.has(key)),
+    );
+    if (Object.keys(lifecycle).length) fields.scripts = lifecycle;
```
</details>
findings.title: Fix `relevant()`: it compares the whole `scripts` object, not only install lifecycle scripts.

findings.body:
**Resolve both sides of the `.bin` comparison.**

Line 88 compares `dirname(source)` with `resolve(installed, '.bin')`. `fs.promises.cp` passes `source` to `filter` without resolving it. If a caller passes a relative `installed`, such as `node_modules`, `dirname(source)` is relative and the comparison never matches.

The launcher branch is then skipped silently. The original POSIX shims are copied as plain files. This removes the isolation that the comment on Lines 85-87 describes.

`assertAddressDependenciesIsolated` calls `realpath` on its directory argument. This function does not. Resolve `source` before the comparison so the check does not depend on the caller passing an absolute path.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-      if (process.platform !== 'win32' && dirname(source) === resolve(installed, '.bin')) {
+      if (process.platform !== 'win32' && resolve(dirname(source)) === resolve(installed, '.bin')) {
```
</details>
findings.title: Resolve both sides of the `.bin` comparison.
